manifest.name: dsh-thinking-notifier
manifest.description: DeepSeek Harness desktop popup plugin: shows AI thinking status in a bottom-right always-on-top card, and alerts you when the AI requests permission, waits for your choice, or finishes thinking
manifest.author: dsh-thinking-notifier contributors

bundle.text:
# dsh-thinking-notifier 持久挂载通道（dsh.bundle.patch）
#
# 安装后，dsh plugin add 会把本包写入 profile 的 dsh.profile.bundles，
# 重启后由本行挂载。客户端半边（lib/client.js）会由 client-modules 扫描
# 并注入 window.__DSH_BOOT__，在浏览器中显示右下角思考状态悬浮窗。
- insert:
    - id: dsh-thinking-notifier
      name: 'dsh-thinking-notifier'

readme.text:
A [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that shows a small **always-on-top desktop popup** in the bottom-right corner of your screen. It mirrors the AI's thinking status in real time and alerts you when the AI **requests permission**, **waits for a choice from you**, or **finishes thinking** — even when you are working in other apps, browsers, or virtual desktops.

> 中文说明见 [README.zh.md](./README.zh.md)

| State | Popup | Sound |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AI is thinking | DeepSeek-blue pulsing dot + `AI 正在思考…` + elapsed time. Auto-collapses to a 25 px slim right-edge tab after 5 s; hover or click the tab to expand it again | none |
| AI waits for your choice | Violet pulsing dot + `AI 正在等待你的选择` + the question heading, the first question's option labels (`选项：A / B`, `（可多选）` for multi-select, `（共 N 问）` when several questions arrive at once) and how long it has been waiting. Stays expanded until you answer | system Question |
| AI requests permission | Amber pulsing dot + `AI 请求权限` + session/tool name. Stays expanded until you decide | system Exclamation |
| AI finished thinking | Green dot + `AI 已完成思考`, auto-hides after 12 s | system Asterisk |
| Idle | Hidden | none |

- DeepSeek-style dark card (`#1E2235` / `#4D6BFE`).
- Always-on-top frameless window, bottom-right, visible over any application.
- Auto-collapses into a 25 px slim right-edge tab after 5 s while the AI is thinking, so it stays visible without blocking desktop controls.
- Hover or click the edge tab to expand it manually; new turns, questions, permission requests, and completions expand it automatically.
- Click the **X** button to dismiss the current popup; the next new turn, question, permission request, or completion will show it again.
- Questions are shown with their options, which is enough to know what is being decided; the answer itself is still given in the DSH Web UI (the popup is read-only by design).
- Multiple sessions are summarized automatically.
- The popup process stays alive while DSH runs; it exits ~15 s after the status endpoint becomes unreachable.
- No browser extension required; the popup is a native desktop window.

```
DSH process
  └─ lib/index.js (host plugin)
       ├─ listens to session/event: turn/start, turn/end, approval/asked, approval/decided, session/title
       ├─ rebuilds existing session state from ctx.sessions.list() at startup

`GET http://127.0.0.1:7389/status` returns:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "mode": "question",
  "statusText": "AI 正在等待你的选择",

`mode` priority: `pending` (an approval is waiting) > `question` (a question is waiting) > `running` > `done` (shown for 12 s) > `idle`.
`pendingKind` is `approval` or `question`. `timeText` is the thinking timer while `running` and the waiting time while `question`; `detailText` carries the first question's options.

```sh
cd dsh-thinking-notifier
dsh plugin --profile web add .

readme.section: Restart DSH web so the host plugin is loaded

readme.text:
```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-thinking-notifier
dsh web
```

| Environment variable | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DSH_THINKING_NOTIFIER_PORT` | `7389` | Local status server port. If busy, the next 10 ports are tried. |
| `DSH_THINKING_NOTIFIER_NO_POPUP` | unset | Set to `1` to run the status server without launching the desktop popup (headless, tests). |

- DeepSeek Harness Web UI (`dsh web`)
- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`
- Windows: Windows 10/11 with PowerShell 5.1+ (built in)
- macOS/Linux: Python 3 with `tkinter`

| Area | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Thinking / done states, popup geometry, sounds, single instance | verified on Windows 10/11 (PowerShell 5.1 + WPF) |
| Question state (`ask_user_question`) | verified end to end in a live DSH session (a real question drove the popup into the waiting state, and it cleared when the answer arrived), against the real `ctx.userQuestions` service in a cordis context, and by the smoke test |
| Permission alert (amber) | **verified only with the mock status service.** On a Windows DSH install without a confining sandbox, an out-of-workspace write is not intercepted, so no approval is raised by the runtime; the request only appears when a tool call explicitly asks for a `sandbox_permissions` escalation or a pre-execute hook returns `ask` |
| `desktop-popup.py` (macOS/Linux) | **never run on real hardware** — syntax-checked only |
| Popup process stacking after repeated `dsh web` restarts | the launcher kills stale popups for its own port before starting a new one; verified for a single restart cycle |

readme.section: status-machine smoke test (fake cordis context, no popup, port 17389)
render the popup against a mock status service, on a spare port
readme.text:
node tools/mock-status.mjs question --port 17389
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File desktop-popup.ps1 -Port 17389   # Windows
python3 desktop-popup.py --port 17389                                               # macOS/Linux
```

Use a spare port for popup experiments: the real popup on `7389` is left alone, because the plugin only cleans up popup processes belonging to its own port.

```
dsh-thinking-notifier/
├── lib/
│   └── index.js          # host plugin: state machine + status service + popup launcher
├── desktop-popup.ps1     # Windows native popup (PowerShell + WPF)

Debug logs are written to:

- `~/.dsh/tn-plugin.log` — host plugin lifecycle, popup launcher, question watcher.
- `~/.dsh/tn-launcher.log` — PID of the popup process created by the launcher.
- `~/.dsh/tn-popup-debug.log` — popup script lifecycle and polling errors.

If the popup does not appear after restarting `dsh web`, check those logs first.
Note that `popup launcher exit: code=0` in `tn-plugin.log` is expected: the plugin spawns a one-shot launcher which starts the real popup process and then exits.
